#Part A: Basic Operations
#A1 Create v as the sequence 5,10,15...50 using seq().Print its lenght,sum and mean.
```{r}
v <-seq(5:50)
length(5:50)
sum(5:50)
mean(5:50)
```
#A2 Create w that repeats the vector c(1,2,3) four times, and z that repeats each element of c(1,2,3) four times.Print both.
```{r}
w <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), times = 4)
z <- rep(c(1, 2, 3), each = 4)

print(w)
print(z)

```
#A3 Compute and print: the remaider of 17 divided by 5, the integer division of 17 by 5,2 to the power of 10, the square root of 144, and pi rounded to 3 decimals.
```{r}

rem <- 17 %% 5
int_div <- 17 %/% 5
power_val <- 2 ^ 10
sqrt_val <- sqrt(144)
pi_rounded <- round(pi, digits = 3)

print(rem)
print(int_div)
print(power_val)
print(sqrt_val)
print(pi_rounded)

```
#A4 Given a <- c(2,4,6,8) and b <- c(1,3,5,7), print a+b, a*b, the logical comparison a>b, and the dot product sum(a*b).
```{r}

a <- c(2, 4, 6, 8)
b <- c(1, 3, 5, 7)


print(a + b)
print(a * b)
print(a > b)
print(sum(a * b))

```

#A5 Use paste() to produce "Student-1" "Student-2" "Student-3". Then identify the datatype of 42,42L,"42",41i, and TRUE. What are its output?
```{r}
students <- paste("Student", 1:3, sep = "-")
print(students)


print(class(42))
print(class(42L))
print(class("42"))
print(class(41i))
print(class(TRUE))

```

#Part B: Data Frames and Conditional Statements

#B1 Create a data frame students with 8 rows and these columns(use stringsAsFactors+ FALSE;sex is "M" or "F")
```{r}
students <- data.frame(
  student_id = 1:8,
  name = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana",
           "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section = c("A","B","A","C","B","C","A","B"),
  midterm = c(78,85,92,67,74,88,95,59),
  final = c(82,79,96,71,80,91,93,65),
  attendance = c(95,88,100,72,90,85,98,60),
  
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

students
```

#B2 Display the structure, dimension, column names, and summary of students
```{r}
str(students)
dim(students)
names(students)
summary(students)
```

#B3 Add a column average = the mean of midterm and final for each student, rounded to 1 decimal
```{r}
students$average <- round((students$midterm + students$final) / 2, 1)
students
```

#B4 Add a logical column passed that is TRUE when average >=70 and attendance >=75
```{r}
students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75
students
```
#B5 Using ifelse(), add a colum standing with these values based on average
#"Honors" if average >=90
#"Good" if average >= 75(and below 90)
#"Needs Support" otherwise
```{r}
students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                     ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good",
                            "Needs Support"))

students
```
#B6 Write a function classify(score) that uses an if/ else if/ else chain and return "Distinction" for 85 or above,"Merit" for 70 to 84,"Pass" for 50 to 69, and "Fail" below 50. Test it with sapply(c(90,73,55,40), classify) and print the result.
```{r}
classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    return("Distinction")
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    return("Merit")
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    return("Pass")
  } else {
    return("Fail")
  }
}

result <- sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)
print(result)
```

#Part C: rbind() and cbind()
#C1 Create a data frame new_students with two students. Its columns must match the original, including average, passed and standing, computed the same way:
id 9, Ines, F, section C, midterm 81, final 84, attendance 92
id 10, Jamal, M, section A, midterm 70, final 68, attendance 80

use rbind() to append them to students, saving the results as students_all.
```{r}
new_students <- data.frame(
  student_id = c(9, 10),
  name = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex = c("F", "M"),
  section = c("C", "A"),
  midterm = c(81, 70),
  final = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

new_students$average <- round(
  (new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2, 1
)

new_students$passed <- new_students$average >= 70 &
                       new_students$attendance >= 75

new_students$standing <- ifelse(
  new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
  ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support")
  
)

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)

print(students_all)
View(students_all)
```

#C2 Create the numeric vector quiz <- c(8,7,10,6,7,9,10,5,8,6). Use cbind() to attach it to students_all as a column named quiz.Confirm the result is still a data frame with class().

```{r}

quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)

students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz)
print(students_all)
class(students_all)
```

#C3 Create the matrix m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final) and use rbind() to append a final row containing the column means, labelled "mean".

```{r}
m <- cbind(
  midterm = students_all$midterm,
  final = students_all$final
)

m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))
print(m)
```
#C4 In a comment(2-3 sentences), expalin what error rbind() produces if the data frames have different column names, and show the output if you safely catch it with tryCatch()

tryCatch(rbind(students, bad), error = function(e) { message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e));NULL}).
```{r}
# rbind() produces an error when data frames have different column names.
# It requires matching column names and their order to combine rows.
# tryCatch() safely catches the error and displays the error message.

result <- tryCatch(
  rbind(students, bad),
  error = function(e) {
    message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)

print(result)
```
#Part D: Subsetting
Use students_all(with quiz) for all question. Print every result.

#D1 Extract the name column in three ways: $,[["name"]], and [,"name"].
```{r}

students_all$name


students_all[["name"]]
students_all[, "name"]
```

#D2 Extract rows 2 to 5 and only the column name, midterm, final.
```{r}

students_all[2:5, c("name", "midterm", "final")]
```
#D3 Using logical subsetting, select students with attendance above 90.
```{r}
high_attendance <- students_all[students_all$attendance > 90, ]
print(high_attendance)
```

#D4 Using subset(), select student sex "F" in section "A" or "C" whose final is at least 75; return only name,section and final
```{r}
result <- subset(
  students_all,
  sex == "F" & section %in% c("A", "C") & final >= 75,
  select = c(name, section, final)
)

print(result)
```

#D5 Use which.max() and which.min() to report the name of the student with the highest and lowest average.
```{r}
highest <- which.max(students_all$average)

lowest <- which.min(students_all$average)

cat("Highest average:", students_all$name[highest],
    "-", students_all$average[highest], "\n")

cat("Lowest average:", students_all$name[lowest],
    "-", students_all$average[lowest], "\n")
```

#D6 Sort students_all by average in descending order, then print the top 3 rows.
```{r}

students_sorted <- students_all[
  order(students_all$average, decreasing = TRUE),
]

print(head(students_sorted, 3))
```
